approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted scored molecules, using score-band parent selection, connected-fragment crossover and ordinary local mutations. Stable canonical admission builds a fresh surplus pool. A Gaussian process learns from the complete earlier accepted archive using folded counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity. It centers and scales the raw scores, then uses correlated posterior draws to choose which pool members receive evaluation. Real raw scores update the greedy breeding population, archive and incumbent.
approach.novelty: Change only the values the surrogate learns: map each accepted score to the standard-normal quantile of its average rank, preserving exact ties, then apply the inherited centering and scaling. This replaces sensitivity to cardinal score gaps with guidance based on relative order. Raw scores still govern survival, parent ranking and reported outcomes. Current siblings established the value of the full selector but found that residual scaling and removing fingerprint folding could improve diagnostic measures while losing endpoint score. This target transform tests a different part of the retained selector. Its predictions describe latent ranks, and its benefit must be established by complete search outcomes.

observed_bottleneck: The useful current composite selector still fits standardized cardinal scores, so unequal raw score gaps determine its regression targets even though the endpoint objective is a maximum. This is an untested target-geometry limitation, not an established cause of poor search. The actual n-62daf219c70a summaries and run logs show all 15 current-profile sessions complete, 4,500 evaluations including 4,350 accepted offspring, macro mean 0.5956696497334577 and population SD 0.02659287062806747. A read-only fixed-data audit of its 435 actual fits, 65,250 accepted training occurrences, recorded pools and original normal arrays independently reconstructs the raw-target model and every original selected order. There are exact score ties in 370 fits, accounting for 9,870 tied training occurrences; the largest tie block has 13 records and no actual fit is all-equal. All 435 standardized target vectors change under the issued midrank-normal formula. The maximum absolute per-archive standardized target changes from 8.64540050130548 for raw scores to 2.95951042141564 for rank targets. This describes target geometry, not accuracy or calibrated uncertainty. On these same fixed inputs the transform changes all 435 selected orders, 434 sets and 2,831 ordered positions; 2,769 choices differ on the original raw-model availability masks. One batch changes order only. The unchanged raw reference reconstructs saved means/SDs/draws within 9.34e-14/5.11e-15/1.05e-13; independent pairwise ranks and inverse CDF agree within 1.34e-15. These are unscored same-state alternatives, not a Child rollout. n-01b48dd09404 removes predictive influence while retaining full pools and computations, loses 0.12438789088524467 on the complete matched mean, and loses 13 of 15 endpoints while two improve. That supports the composite module under these conditions without attributing its value to a particular target geometry. n-e00db808bbb4 removes occurrence multiplicity, loses 0.051295849138213355 on all three seed macros with three contrary task-seed gains, and reproduces historical binary trajectories rather than adding independent seeds. The direct counterexamples remain: n-38bcd7569cce increases same-selected-stream coverage from 77.91% to 90.69% yet loses 0.03814118675118202 in endpoint mean; all seed macros fall while eight task-seed endpoints improve. n-b14daceabbeb changes all 435 kernels and 392 same-pool selected sets and modestly improves selected-stream MSE/rank/coverage, yet loses 0.04816296717262832, again on every seed macro, with six task-seed gains. All three median_2 prediction MSEs worsen despite endpoint gains. Those negative amplitude and unfolding variants neither refute retained residual/count presence nor establish that ordinal targets help. The new hypothesis is that replacing cardinal spacing changes learned relative ordering and subsequent allocation usefully; loss of important rare high-score gaps and remapping of earlier ranks remain explicit risks.
hypothesis: Replace raw accepted-score regression targets inside the retained count-GP selector with deterministic standard-normal midrank targets, preserving exact score ties and applying the inherited centering and population-SD normalization, while all search-state updates and endpoints continue to use real raw scores.

finding_summary.headline: Rank targets change every selected batch but reduce ordering correlation and mean endpoint score
finding_summary.insights: The missing benefit is not explained by an unexposed transformation or unchanged choices: ordinal targets alter the entire panel, but their registered ordering advantage fails. Preserving observed label order is insufficient to preserve useful cardinal spacing or improve prediction on newly selected molecules. Even so, all three median_2 endpoints improve while their ordering correlations worsen, and raw parent beats and incumbent gains rise from 629/258 to 655/272 despite the lower overall endpoint mean. Those counterexamples prevent treating ordering correlation or local gains as complete explanations of search utility. Six distinct-molecule pool pairs still share both folded and native count vectors. Conventional aryl amines and carbonyl families remain useful alongside reactive bonds, complex rings and unspecified stereochemistry; target remapping does not repair those chemistry or identity limits. Latent uncertainty has no established raw-score calibration, and no raw-unit error or coverage proxy is substituted. This is a negative result for the rank-target increment on this composition, while the earlier positive evidence for the composite selector remains intact; the role of lost cardinal gaps and later adaptive paths is unresolved.
finding_summary.results: The exact tie-preserving map changes all 435 fitted target vectors and all 435 selected sets. All latent models, raw-reference controls and raw-feedback joins reconstruct; normalized covariance and original random draws remain unchanged on identical inputs. Yet mean within-batch ordering correlation falls from the raw reference’s 0.484299 to 0.443166 on the same scored molecules. Mean raw endpoint falls from 0.595670 to 0.574603, a loss of 0.021067 instead of the required 0.002 gain. Seed macro changes are -0.043227, +0.022366 and -0.042341. Six task-seed endpoints improve and nine decline; all three median_2 endpoints improve. Macro dispersion decreases from 0.026593 to 0.011472. Every evaluation completes.

molecular.headline: Flexible aryl amines and compact carbonyl rings coexist with N-halogen chemistry, repeated heterocycles and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent trajectories were read: 4,500 observations per node, including 4,350 optimizer proposals per node. Every supplied task and Search Seed 0, 1 and 2 is covered; no listed path is missing. The brief reports complete profile-matched pairing to n-62daf219c70a at 300 observations per task and ten-member batches. The output includes halogen-free indole carboxamides with an acyclic allenyl ether, N-halogenated hydrazide/amide series, large repeated azaheterocyclic diones, cyanate/formate-substituted heteroarenes, conventional flexible aryl amines, spiro cyclic amines, medium-ring nitrogen/carbonyl assemblies and compact fluorinated dione heterocycles. Proposal ring-digit incidence spans 0.9678 to 0.9908 and aromatic-string incidence 0.8759 to 0.9885. These support abundant rings and aromatic-labelled output, not validated geometry or independent scaffold coverage. Diversity is moderate across evaluated seed families, with recurring leading series within seeds. Moderate drug-likeness reflects recognizable aryl/amine/amide architectures, not computed properties or validation of reactive members. Synthetic plausibility remains questionable because of direct heteroatom-halogen bonds, unusual unsaturation and complex ring topology. All tasks have stereocentre-string and charge-string incidence 0.0 despite potential stereogenic centres and available basic amines. Sizes below are SMILES heavy-atom-token counts. All cited scores are accepted raw trajectory scores and raw endpoints, distinct from the stated latent standard-normal midrank targets and rank-space posterior means or uncertainties; no raw-unit calibration claim follows. A leader means an evaluated raw-score maximum whose value agrees with best_so_far. Tied structures remain separate evidence, without claiming which one remained a breeding parent. Initial observations and late proposals are labelled separately; the trajectories do not establish breeding-population retention or unselected-pool exposure. Raw-score ties do not establish count aliases; folded-bin aliases, native-hash equivalence and count-vector equivalence are distinct from molecular identity. Indexed historical molecular assessments n-e00db808bbb4 and n-b14daceabbeb already describe conventional leaders mixed with reactive output under count removal and unfolding. They are condition-bound context, not additional current replicas or proof that rank targets remove aliasing. This report makes no activation, eligibility or mediation judgement.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 0 reaches a 24-atom halogen-free indole carboxamide with methyl groups, an N-pyridyl substituent and an acyclic allenyl ether. Two pyridyl nitrogen positions share the highest raw score. The indole and amide are recognizable chemistry; this acyclic allene is not a strained cyclic cumulene. Seed 1 has tied 25-atom leaders: an N-chlorinated indole-like ring with an N-chlorinated phenyl hydrazide, and a vinyl/methoxy relative with an N-S amide substituent. Seed 2 reaches tied 26-atom N-halogenated carboxamides with N-bromo amides, bromomethyl pyridyl groups and ring N-F or N-Br. Ordinary aryl amide organization therefore coexists with reactive local environments. Mean proposal SMILES length is 42.2, halogen-string incidence 0.7494 and cumulated-double-bond incidence 0.1149; the last number includes acyclic chemistry and is not a count of infeasible rings.
liabilities: Direct N-Cl, N-Br and N-F, N-N/N-S linkages and bromomethyl groups are chemically distinct from conventional aryl halides.
Allenyl ethers and the much more unusual sulfur-cumulene late proposal require different environment-specific assessments.
The high-scoring halogen-free indole amide prevents treating reactive heteroatom-halogen chemistry as unavoidable.
missing_features: The favorable aryl/carboxamide context is present, but conventional alternatives to N-halogenated and N-S environments at the exact leading scores are not consistently established across seeds.
Chemical-state and stability characterization is missing for the allenyl-ether series, without implying that its acyclic unsaturation is geometrically impossible.
Evaluated leading alternatives are often close relatives; constitutional variation does not by itself establish independent fingerprint or pool coverage.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial indole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145. Seed-0 leaders observed at evaluations 108 and 221 both score 0.4572645941803378; seed-1 tied leaders score 0.44989726212142783 and seed-2 tied leaders 0.42408253349563446. A close seed-0 allenyl ether scores 0.4126819838532174 versus 0.3057223329855419 for its allyl-ether counterpart. This supports local unsaturation sensitivity, not a universal missing-group prescription. In seed 1, chloromethoxy-to-methoxy replacement raises 0.42218506297789204 to 0.44989726212142783 while other liabilities remain. Isolated F scores 0.0. The final seed-0 sulfur-containing cumulene/carbamate proposal scores 2.353859395444973e-05 while best_so_far remains 0.4572645941803378; it did not replace the numeric benchmark incumbent. Parent endpoints are 0.39405142067435733, 0.47411701813450596 and 0.438972502037081: the seed-0 gain coexists with two decreases. Exact raw ties between different molecules do not identify identical count vectors or latent predictions.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 0 produces tied 51- and 52-atom leaders containing two fused nitrogen/dione units linked through a large aromatic-labelled diaza ring, with N-formyl substitution and brominated imine-containing chains. Seed 1 has a 37-atom leader with an azaheterocyclic carbonyl/oxygen ring, biaryl/pyridyl regions, an aryl cyanate and formate esters. Ethyl-to-propyl and methoxy-to-chloromethoxy relatives tie its raw score; the methoxy leader contains no halogen. Seed 2 reaches a 46-atom dione/enamine assembly bearing a pentanoyl aryl group, propyl carbonate, another azaarene, fluoromethyl groups and an N-O-fluoroalkyl substituent. The latter has N-O-C-F connectivity, not an O-F bond. Mean proposal SMILES length is 88.0, cumulated-double-bond incidence 0.0690, aromatic-string incidence 0.9782 and ring-digit incidence 0.9793. Some series are very large repeated heterocycles; the seed-1 family is a less enlarged heteroaromatic alternative.
liabilities: Large aromatic-labelled diaza rings and repeated heterocyclic units pose geometry and synthesis questions unresolved by SMILES notation.
Aryl cyanates, formate/carbonate esters, brominated imine chains and N-O-linked substituents need local stability assessment.
Large assemblies lack a uniform endpoint advantage, but the evidence supports neither a fixed size cap nor automatic growth.
missing_features: Compact stable alternatives to repeated diones, large aromatic-labelled rings and heavily decorated linkers are not consistently demonstrated among the evaluated leaders.

Conventional local environments are incompletely maintained around cyanates, N-O-alkyl, imine and haloalkyl groups; the two chloromethyl/methyl ties show context-specific alternatives already available.
Imine geometry, tautomer identity and physical feasibility of the large diaza-ring representation remain unestablished.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.548381482770623 and an early peroxide-substituted quinoline 0.5100965759438103; ketene alone scores the observed floor of 0.5. Raw endpoints are 0.6172155903926363, 0.6200625177607275 and 0.6130107215299914. Seed-1 methoxy and chloromethoxy variants both score 0.6200625177607275. In seed 2, N-O-chloromethyl-to-N-O-methyl replacement leaves 0.6101821439235593 unchanged. Thus the chloromethyl additions supply no observed reward in these specific contexts. Parent endpoints are 0.8561477222467935, 0.6248206599713055 and 0.6178024026512013, with 30-, 32- and 37-atom leaders. All Child endpoints are lower despite larger leaders; size is an association, not an established cause. The Parent seed-0 thione/O-F/halomethyl family also had liabilities. Aromatic/carbonyl organization matters more visibly than halogen atoms alone, but no unique missing target motif is established.

per_task.generated_character: Seed-0 leaders have 25 atoms and are comparatively conventional flexible diaryl compounds with a primary aminomethyl branch, a secondary amine, phenol and methoxy or methylthio substitution. Their halogens are carbon-bound. Seed 1 has tied 25-atom cyclic-amine leaders with two N-methyl saturated nitrogen centres, a spiro small nitrogen ring and a benzene-fused small carbocycle. Seed 2 has 28-atom aminoethyl/aniline/thioether arenes connected through a cycloheptadiene region to a haloaryl benzylic chloride or fluoride; a methyl analogue avoids that benzylic halide. Mean proposal SMILES length is 52.1 and halogen incidence 0.9816. Useful primary, secondary and tertiary amines are present. The flexible seed-0 family shows that unusual sulfur valence, direct N-halogen bonds and crowded bridges are not required throughout the strong evaluated output, while constrained seed families retain geometric and stereochemical uncertainty.
liabilities: Benzylic chloride and the late aryl S-F group raise distinct reactivity concerns.
Spiro small nitrogen rings and benzene-fused small carbocycles require geometric and stereochemical assessment; these motifs are not automatically infeasible.
Flexibility, aromatic surface and multiple basic centres are not characterized here for solubility or selectivity.
missing_features: Stereochemical identity is unresolved at the flexible leader's substituted carbon and in saturated, spiro and benzylic environments elsewhere.
Protonation states are not explicit, but basic centres are abundant; absent charge markers do not support simply adding another amine.
Conventional bond environments are not maintained in every high-scoring relative, despite ordinary flexible-amine and halogen-free counterexamples.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: An N-sulfonyl cyclic amine scores 0.00021169315013374197. Seed-0 methoxy, methylthio and halogen variants tie at 0.9999983538232358. Seed-1 fluoro and bromo variants tie at 0.9999966831838307; a late halogen-free relative scores 0.9964854387957327. Seed-2 benzylic chloride/fluoride leaders tie at 0.9939135632601879, and a methyl counterpart scores 0.9745195157496904. A smaller aryl/amine proposal lacking the larger cyclic context scores 0.2212052222998651, so amine presence alone is insufficient. Conversely, a late aryl S-F derivative scores 0.9949550350657417, showing that a near-ceiling raw value does not validate every bond environment. Parent endpoints are 0.9999989177995104, 0.9969753164881906 and 0.9999934235240012: seed 1 improves, seed 0 is numerically very close but lower, and seed 2 decreases. These are raw-score associations with available amines and aromatic organization, not measured selectivity or evidence of representation equivalence.

per_task.generated_character: Seed leaders contain 32, 34 and 32 atoms. Seed 0 combines a propyl-substituted azaarene with an O-CH2-O bridge, an ethylphenyl group and an eight-membered nitrogen/dicarbonyl ring. It has recognizable ureide/amide functionality without direct heteroatom-halogen bonds. Seed 1 uses an extended fused aromatic/pyrazole-like system connected to a larger nitrogen-rich ring with a carbonyl, ethoxy, propyl and N-methyl groups. Seed 2 joins propylquinoline to a pyrazole-containing nitrogen/dicarbonyl ring with an N-N segment. Carbonyl count and ring topology vary across the successful families. Aromatic-string incidence is 0.9885, ring-digit incidence 0.9908, halogen incidence 0.1253 and cumulated-double-bond incidence 0.0; mean SMILES length is 55.9. This is ring-rich chemistry without reliance on cumulative unsaturation or heavy halogen decoration.
liabilities: Large nitrogen rings and the extended fused seed-1 architecture pose synthesis and geometry questions despite recognizable constituent groups.
The seed-2 N-N bond needs local assessment, but the near-scoring carbon counterpart shows that bond is not uniquely necessary for similar performance.
Low-scoring large assemblies and tiny fragments show lost molecular context; they do not identify breeding-population survivors.
missing_features: Specified stereochemistry and established conformations are missing for saturated junctions and the larger nitrogen/carbonyl rings.
Simpler feasible connectivities at each exact leading score are not consistently demonstrated; close homologues and the carbon-for-nitrogen example are partial counterexamples.
No exact absent target motif is identifiable, and adding rings, halogens or cumulative unsaturation indiscriminately is unsupported.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329, a 55-atom repeated heterocyclic assembly 0.12681166987198764 and acetylene 0.0. Leaders reach 0.24508530837529843, 0.2312044925451128 and 0.22800192351525037, all above Parent endpoints of 0.2258403994203931, 0.2214095461892601 and 0.22600312875247064. The seed-0 gain uses fewer atoms than its 34-atom Parent leader; the other Child leaders exceed Parent sizes of 32 and 29 atoms. No uniform size explanation follows. A seed-0 methyl homologue scores 0.24337203591948736 and a shorter seed-1 nitrogen-ring relative 0.22784329769824466. Replacing one nitrogen in the seed-2 N-N segment with carbon gives 0.22768118931934517, close to 0.22800192351525037 while removing that particular N-N bond. Combined aromatic and nitrogen/carbonyl context associates with reward, without making every heteroatom or bridge indispensable. The all-seed gains remain valid descriptive counterexamples despite unresolved chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: All seed leaders contain 26 atoms. Seed 0 has a non-aromatic-written partly saturated dione heterobicycle, N-F, a fluorinated diene chain and an enolic nitrogen ring with fluoromethyl substitution. This high-scoring example has no lowercase aromatic atoms. Seed 1 has a more recognizable fused nitrogen dione with N-methyl/N-F, aminophenyl and difluorocyclobutyl groups. Seed 2 combines a related small-ring dione heterobicycle with a hydroxylated fluoro/methyl azaarene and a monofluorocyclobutyl substituent. Small fluorinated rings are not automatically infeasible, but their stereochemistry is unspecified. Mean SMILES length is 50.6, aromatic-string incidence 0.8759, ring-digit incidence 0.9678 and cumulated-double-bond incidence 0.0333. Current leaders differ from the Parent seed-2 cyclic-cumulene family while retaining other state and bond-environment concerns.
liabilities: Direct N-F remains common among leaders, and partly saturated fused small-ring arrangements require geometry assessment.
Enolic nitrogen rings, fluorinated unsaturated chains and unspecified small-ring configurations leave stability and molecular-state questions.
Poor repeated heterocycles and fragments are evaluated proposals, not evidence that low raw values replaced better numeric incumbents.
missing_features: Stable local environments are not consistently established at the exact leading scores, although the strong N-F-free relative is a specific partial counterexample.
Fluorocyclobutyl and fused-ring stereochemistry, alkene geometry and enol/imino tautomer identity remain unresolved.
The scores identify neither a single absent target motif nor a universal need for more fluorine, aromaticity or cyclic cumulenes.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.0020944534688323298, a 53-atom repeated heterocycle 1.4497754218643327e-29 and isolated F 1.1043196211273875e-26. Leaders reach 0.5913627040251141, 0.6149989708737519 and 0.5329435590162632. Removing an aryl fluorine from the 27-atom seed-1 difluorocyclobutyl family raises 0.6049028215927195 to 0.6149989708737519; more fluorine is not uniformly advantageous. N-F-to-N-methyl changes vary in magnitude: one fixed seed-0 framework changes 0.5434853516047222 to 0.5404578277559989, another 0.5087154276568817 to 0.2712101222951787. The N-F-free 0.5404578277559989 example limits universal necessity; the larger decrease prevents claiming uniformly harmless replacement. The final seed-0 C=NF fragment scores 7.411552050139358e-20 while best_so_far stays 0.5913627040251141. Parent endpoints are 0.6510211907030741, 0.4870057305679067 and 0.7208853668418119. The substantial seed-1 gain coexists with two decreases. Reward associates with compact fluorinated/polar context, not a demonstrated exact pharmacophore or physical stability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c through its reproduced baseline n-62daf219c70a and is newly observed in n-ae12ccae8c7b on three supplied Search Seeds, 300 observations per task and ten-member batches. Current output includes N-Cl/N-Br/N-F, N-N/N-S and N-O-linked substituents, cyanates, haloalkyl groups and a high-scoring aryl S-F relative. Counterexamples include a halogen-free indole amide, ordinary flexible primary/secondary aryl amines near the raw score ceiling, and chloromethyl-to-methyl replacements with unchanged or increased scores. One N-F-free analogue scores 0.5404578277559989 versus 0.5434853516047222, but another N-F-to-N-methyl change lowers 0.5087154276568817 to 0.2712101222951787. Neither conventional nor reactive chemistry is uniformly rewarded.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional bond environments within otherwise useful aromatic, amine and carbonyl organization.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer conventional alternatives while preserving favorable relationships learned from accepted task-local feedback. Distinguish carbon-bound halogens from heteroatom-halogen bonds and interpret sulfur, nitrogen and oxygen by full environment. This motivates conditional chemical control, not an element ban or guaranteed scoring benefit from a filter; latent rank uncertainty is not a raw-unit chemical reward estimate.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This geometry gap is inherited from n-c55c3d520a2c via n-62daf219c70a and persists as large aromatic-labelled diaza rings, spiro small nitrogen rings, extended fused systems and larger nitrogen/carbonyl closures. Ring digits and aromatic labels do not establish feasibility. Boundaries include conventional flexible aryl amines, recognizable medium-ring carbonyl functionality and saturated fluorocyclobutyl groups. The high-scoring acyclic allenyl ether is not the same concern as a small cyclic cumulene; one complete task's proposals contain no cumulated-double-bond strings. These are chemical observations under the current matched panel, not component attribution.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently establish credible geometry and molecular state for complex fused, bridged and extended ring output.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Assess ring size, bridge connectivity, unsaturation and chemical state in their specific environments while retaining access to ordinary small, fused and saturated rings. Explore feasible alternatives preserving favorable functional organization. Ring counts and blanket bans on allenes, rings or growth cannot supply the missing information; no guaranteed score benefit is established.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This identity gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c, reproduced by n-62daf219c70a and re-observed in the current complete panel. All tasks have stereocentre-string incidence 0.0 despite substituted aminomethyl-bearing carbons, benzylic halides, spiro junctions and fluorinated saturated rings. Charge-string incidence is also 0.0, but available basic amines are abundant. The evidence establishes unspecified identity rather than a measured penalty for a particular stereoisomer or protonation state.
transferable_gaps.gap: Potentially stereogenic saturated centres and ring junctions remain without explicit stereochemical identity in the output.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or resolve stereochemistry where constitution requires it, allowing for achiral and configurationally unstable cases. Treat protonation, alkene geometry and tautomerism separately. Neither raw-score ties nor count-vector or native-hash equality certifies complete molecular identity, and no objective-specific state prescription follows.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap is inherited from n-c55c3d520a2c through n-62daf219c70a and has fresh evaluated-output evidence at the current three-seed budget. Late fragments can score near the observed floor while the numeric incumbent stays high, and large repeated heterocycles can score below compact leaders. Counterexamples include compact flexible aryl amines near the ceiling, all-three nitrogen/carbonyl family gains with mixed size changes, and a substantial positive seed exception in a compact fluorinated dione family. Indexed count-removal and unfolding assessments also contain conventional leaders and mixed chemical outcomes; they do not establish a universal size or representation rule.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve productive molecular context while controlling fragmentation and repeated scaffold elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use accepted task-local evidence to preserve favorable relationships during simplification, growth and scaffold replacement, evaluating independent alternatives for usefulness and plausibility. Distinguish evaluated molecules, raw-score incumbents and documented breeding survivors. Do not infer unselected-pool exposure or molecular diversity from this record or native hashes. Chemical alternatives are not automatically better endpoints, and these associations do not explain mediation by rank targets.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Score-quantile parent allocation, previously accepted scored parents, bounded greedy survival and the full accepted-score archive.
Connected-fragment crossover with unchanged post-crossover mutation probability and multi-parent opportunities.
Ordinary single-atom replacement plus append, delete, insert, bond-change, ring-open and ring-close mutations, with inherited walk and saturation laws.
Sanitization, stable canonical identity admission, initial/emitted and temporary-pool duplicate rejection, bounded retries and fixed surplus pools.

Folded integer-count Morgan features and generalized Tanimoto covariance; all accepted raw archive records; fixed GP normalization/noise/jitter/full covariance. Target normalization now acts on exact normal-midrank latent labels within the composite selector.

Original correlated posterior normal draws, residual influence, available masks and stable first-index ties; identity-bound latent predictions, explicit raw-reference diagnostics and next-fit mapping-version probes. Raw breeding/survival/incumbent feedback remains unchanged.
Passive aromatic-pair enumeration and the unreachable direct-exchange implementation retained for controlled attribution.
Fresh objective-local state, deterministic prepared settings, ten-member announced batches and protocol-owned budgets/resources.
